answer: The harbour master logs every pilot boarding with the ship, the pilot and the hour, so each arrival is proved guided into port. A basalt boarding claimed as logged fails the log: the pilot must have climbed aboard at the whisper of the harbour, and a boarding never logged has no pilot to answer for the ship. Faking a pilot season means bribing the harbour master, forging one hundred boardings and paying 19,500, while the copper log is read at every inquiry, so a ship whose pilot was never logged pays the wreck herself.
